about: The epistle of the formulary “6th Sunday after Pentecost” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: Brothers, all of us who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into His death. For we were buried with Him through baptism into death, so that, just as Christ rose from the dead through the glory of the Father, we too might walk in newness of life. For if we have become united with Him in the likeness of His death, we will also be united with Him in the likeness of His resurrection. We know this: our old self was crucified with Him so that the body of sin might be destroyed and we might no longer serve sin. For whoever has died has been freed from sin. But if we have died with Christ, we believe that we will also live together with Christ, knowing that Christ, risen from the dead, no longer dies, and death will no longer rule over Him. For the death He died, He died to sin once for all, but the life He lives, He lives to God. So you too must consider yourselves dead to sin, but alive to God in Christ Jesus our Lord.

a.g: might walk in newness of life
we will also be united in the likeness of His resurrection
the body of sin might be destroyed
will no longer rule over Him

ex.w040: The image of planting together expresses union with Christ in His death. The following promise carries the same comparison forward to His resurrection.
ex.w072: The Latin speaks of being justified from sin. Here the surrounding contrast between serving sin and living with Christ brings out release from sin’s claim.
ex.w092: Christ’s rising here is the resurrection already accomplished. The following words affirm that He no longer dies and that death will no longer rule over Him.
